# CDDL to Zig mapping

This document defines exactly what `cddl-zig generate` emits for each CDDL construct.
The emitted storage types hold the data; the emitted codecs enforce every
constraint that the storage type cannot express. The storage type never stands in
for a check: `0..10` stored as `u8` is still checked to be at most 10.

Supported and unsupported constructs are listed in [standards.md](standards.md).
The pipeline and runtime are described in [architecture.md](architecture.md).

## Generated module

`generate` writes one Zig source file:

```zig
// Code generated by cddl-zig from schema.cddl. DO NOT EDIT.
// Runtime ABI: 1. Source SHA-256: <64 lowercase hex digits>.

const std = @import("std");
const rt = @import("cddl_runtime");

comptime {
    if (rt.abi_version != 1) @compileError("cddl_runtime ABI mismatch: generated for ABI 1");
}

pub const types = struct {
    // One declaration per generated type, in source order.
};

pub const codecs = struct {
    // One namespace per type (not per group struct), in the same order.
};

pub const Root = codecs.Message;

pub const Feature = struct { ... }; // only when `.feature` is used
pub const features = [_]Feature{ ... };
```

- The header lists the input basenames in argument order. The hash covers each
  input in order as an 8-byte little-endian length followed by the bytes; file
  names are not hashed. `--no-header` leaves out both comment lines.
- `--runtime-import <name>` changes the imported module name. The default is
  `cddl_runtime`.
- `Root` is the codec of the root rule. With `--root`, that is the first `--root`.
  Without it, the root is the first rule in input order, and it must be a
  non-generic type rule. Otherwise generation fails (see
  [standards.md](standards.md#rules-names-and-root)), so successful output always
  declares `Root`.
- Without `--root`, every non-generic user rule is emitted, together with every
  generic instantiation those rules reach. With `--root`, only the rules reachable
  from the named roots are emitted.
- Prelude types that need a named compound type (`number`, `integer`, `decfrac`,
  and so on) are emitted into `types` only when used, after the user types.

### Codec namespace

Every type rule and every emitted prelude compound type has a namespace with the
same name in `codecs`. Group-rule structs have none, because a group is not a data
item.

```zig
pub const Message = struct {
    pub const Type = types.Message;
    pub const Prefix = struct { value: Type, consumed: usize };

    pub fn encode(
        value: *const Type,
        encoder: *rt.Encoder,
        scratch: std.mem.Allocator,
        limits: rt.Limits,
    ) rt.EncodeError!void;
    pub fn decode(
        arena: *std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
        input: []const u8,
        options: rt.DecodeOptions,
        error_offset: ?*usize,
    ) rt.DecodeError!Type;
    pub fn decodePrefix(
        arena: *std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
        input: []const u8,
        options: rt.DecodeOptions,
        error_offset: ?*usize,
    ) rt.DecodeError!Prefix;
};
```

- `encode` is the only way to validate a value. It writes one data item in core
  deterministic encoding, but only after the value has passed every schema check.
  The encoder is built by the runtime: `Encoder.initWriter(*std.Io.Writer)`,
  `Encoder.initFixed([]u8)`, or `Encoder.initList(gpa, *std.ArrayList(u8))`.
  `scratch` is used for sorting map keys computed at run time (through
  `rt.MapBuilder`), for derived-item checks, and for validating the item layout;
  all of it is freed before `encode` returns. `limits` bounds depth, work, and
  scratch bytes. Errors are classified by `rt.errorKind`: `schema_mismatch` for an
  invalid value, `limit` for depth or work, `allocation` for scratch, and
  `output_capacity` for the sink (`OutputCapacityExceeded` or `WriteFailed`).
  Literal-key maps need no scratch for ordering, because their keys are emitted in
  an order computed at generation time.
- `decode` builds `rt.Decoder.init(arena.allocator(), input, options)`, reads one
  data item, and requires the input to be used up. Leftover bytes give
  `TrailingBytes` (class `malformed`).
- `decodePrefix` reads one data item and returns how many bytes it used. Calling
  it again on `input[consumed..]` reads a CBOR sequence.
- `options.limits` bounds the work. `options.require_deterministic` turns on
  deterministic-input mode. After a failure, if `error_offset` is non-null, it
  holds the byte offset where the decoder stopped.
- Codec functions are not generic and take no `anytype`, so referencing them
  forces every generated body to be analyzed.

Types and codecs are kept in separate namespaces so that a schema field named
`encode`, `decode`, or `Type` can never clash with a generated declaration.

## Ownership

| Storage | Owner | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| Definite-length text and byte strings in a decoded value | The input buffer, borrowed | As long as the input. |
| Fixed byte arrays `[N]u8` | The value itself | Copied. |
| Slices for arrays, repeated entries, and map entries; joined indefinite strings; `*const T` recursion links; `rt.Value` trees | The caller's `std.heap.ArenaAllocator` | Until `arena.deinit()` or a reset. |
| Encode scratch (sorting runtime map keys, derived-item checks, layout validation) | The `scratch` allocator argument | Freed before `encode` returns. |

- Generated decoders never free anything themselves. The arena parameter enforces
  region ownership in the type system. A failed decode can leave allocations in
  the arena, and the caller releases them with the arena.
  `Limits.max_allocation_bytes` caps live allocation during one decode.
- To pick a choice alternative, the decoder probes the input without allocating
  and then materializes only the alternative it picked. Rejected alternatives
  allocate nothing.
- To get a value that does not depend on the caller's input buffer, copy the input
  into the same arena before decoding.
- `encode` takes `*const`, never changes the value, and keeps no reference to it
  after returning. A value with a pointer cycle fails with `DepthLimitExceeded`.
- Code that uses the runtime directly (not generated code) follows the runtime's
  own model: results are owned by the caller's allocator and freed with
  `Value.deinit`.

## Names

Every CDDL `id` is split into segments the same way:

1. Split at each `-`, `.`, `_`, `@`, and `$`, dropping the separator.
2. Split again before an uppercase letter that follows a lowercase letter or a
   digit (`fooBar` gives `foo`, `Bar`). Also split before an uppercase letter that
   is followed by a lowercase letter and preceded by an uppercase letter (`COSEKey`
   gives `COSE`, `Key`).
3. Drop empty segments.

| Kind | Form | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Type name | Each segment with its first letter uppercased and the rest lowercased, joined. | `message` → `Message`, `COSE_Sign1` → `CoseSign1`, `tagged-cose` → `TaggedCose` |
| Field, arm, or enum name | Segments lowercased and joined with `_`. | `displayed-step` → `displayed_step`, `alg-ID` → `alg_id` |

- A field, arm, or enum name that is a Zig keyword, names a primitive type (`u8`,
  `i65`, `f16`, `bool`, `type`, `void`, `anyopaque`, `noreturn`, and the rest), is
  one of `true`, `false`, `null`, or `undefined`, or starts with a digit, is
  emitted as `@"name"`.
- If an id has no segments left (for example `$` or `_`), generation reports an
  error.
- When two source names give the same Zig name in one namespace (types, the fields
  of one struct, or the members of one enum), generation reports an error listing
  both source spans. Names are never changed silently. Choice arms are the one
  exception; see [Choices](#choices).
- Synthesized names (`item_<i>`, `key_<n>`, `entries_<k>`, `alt_<i>`, and
  `<Generic>_<k>`) use a separator that the type-name transform never produces, so
  they cannot clash with type names.

## Prelude

| CDDL | Zig storage | Codec checks beyond storage |
|---|---|---|
| `any` | `rt.Value` | Well-formed and valid. |
| `uint` | `u64` | None. |
| `nint` | `i65` | `value <= -1` |
| `int` | `i65` | None; `i65` covers exactly `-2^64..2^64-1`. |
| `bstr`, `bytes` | `[]const u8` | None. |
| `tstr`, `text` | `[]const u8` | UTF-8. |
| `tdate` | `[]const u8` | Tag 0 and UTF-8. The content is not parsed as RFC 3339. |
| `time` | `types.Number` | Tag 1. |
| `number` | `types.Number = union(enum) { int: i65, float: f64 }` | No conversion between integer and float. |
| `biguint`, `bignint` | `[]const u8` | Tag 2 or 3. Bytes are kept as they are, leading zeros included. |
| `bigint` | `union(enum) { biguint: []const u8, bignint: []const u8 }` | |
| `integer` | `union(enum) { int: i65, biguint: []const u8, bignint: []const u8 }` | |
| `unsigned` | `union(enum) { uint: u64, biguint: []const u8 }` | |
| `decfrac`, `bigfloat` | `struct { e10: i65, m: types.Integer }` and `struct { e2: i65, m: types.Integer }` | Tag 4 or 5, and an array of exactly two items. |
| `eb64url`, `eb64legacy`, `eb16`, `cbor-any` | `rt.Value` | Tag 21, 22, 23, or 55799. |
| `encoded-cbor` | `[]const u8` | Tag 24. The content is not decoded; use `.cbor` to check it. |
| `uri`, `b64url`, `b64legacy`, `regexp`, `mime-message` | `[]const u8` | Tag 32 through 36, and UTF-8. The content is not checked further. |
| `float16` | `f16` | |
| `float32`, `float16-32` | `f32` | |
| `float64`, `float32-64`, `float` | `f64` | |
| `false`, `true`, `nil`, `null`, `undefined` | No storage (literal) | |
| `bool` | `bool` | Only `0xf4` and `0xf5`; never the integers 0 or 1. |

A decoded float is widened exactly to the storage width. Storing in `f16` or `f32`
requires the value to be exact at that width, whatever width it arrived in. Encoding
always picks the shortest width that keeps the value.

## Scalars

### Integers

An integer-valued type is stored in the first standard width that contains the
whole range of the statically computed value set. The candidates are `u8`, `u16`,
`u32`, `u64` when the lower bound is at least 0, and `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`,
`i65` otherwise. Ranges, integer literal choices, `uint .size n`, and `.lt`, `.le`,
`.gt`, `.ge` with integer controllers all feed this computation. The exact set is
checked unless it is the whole domain of the storage type.

| CDDL | Storage | Check |
|---|---|---|
| `0..10` | `u8` | `<= 10` |
| `-100...100` | `i8` | `-100 <= x < 100` |
| `0..255` | `u8` | None. |
| `uint .size 3` | `u32` | `< 2^24` |
| `1..5 / 10..20` | `u8` | `x` in `1..5` or `10..20` |
| `uint .lt 1000` | `u16` | `< 1000` |

Wire integers are converted with checked casts. Generated code never applies
`@intCast`, `@enumFromInt`, or `unreachable` to a value derived from input.

### Floats

Float ranges, float literal choices, and float types with comparison controls are
stored as `f64`, unless the target is narrower (`float16 .le 1.0` is stored as
`f16`).

### Literals and singletons

A type whose value set is a single statically known value (a literal, a folded
`.plus`, `.cat`, `.det`, `.printf`, or `.join`, `uint .eq 5`, `#7.22`) has no
storage. The codec emits the constant and checks it on decode.

| Position | Storage |
|---|---|
| Required entry (occurs exactly once) | No field. |
| Optional entry (occurs 0 or 1 times) | `?void`, default `null`. |
| Other occurrence bounds | `u64` count, default `0` when the minimum is 0, checked against the bounds. |
| Choice arm | `void` arm, or an enum member. |

### Strings

| CDDL | Storage | Check |
|---|---|---|
| `tstr` | `[]const u8` | UTF-8. |
| `bstr` | `[]const u8` | None. |
| `bstr .size N`, with N a singleton from 0 to 64 | `[N]u8` | None. |
| `bstr .size N`, with N above 64 | `[]const u8` | `len == N` |
| `tstr .size N`, or any `.size` with a range | `[]const u8` | Length in bytes. |

`.regexp`, `.bits`, `.cbor`, `.cborseq`, and the RFC 9741 conversion operators keep
the target's storage and add checks.

## Occurrence

This applies to every entry in an array, map, or group. For an entry whose type has
storage `T` and whose occurrence bounds are `(min, max)`:

| Bounds | Storage | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `(1, 1)` | `T` | |
| `(0, 1)` | `?T` | `null` |
| `(0, 0)` | No field. | |
| `(n, n)` with `2 <= n <= 16` | `[n]T` | |
| Any other bounds | `[]const T`, length checked | `&.{}` when `min == 0` |

A repeated group spreads its items into the surrounding container. With
`[* (x: uint, y: uint)]` the storage is `[]const struct { x: u64, y: u64 }` and the
wire form is a single array of `2 * len` integers.

## Arrays

- If the array's group has exactly one entry, the array is stored as that entry's
  storage: `[* uint]` → `[]const u64`, `[uint]` → `u64`, `[2*2 tstr]` →
  `[2][]const u8`. If that entry has no storage, the array is `struct {}`.
- Otherwise the array is a struct with one field per entry that has storage, in
  source order. A field takes the entry's label (`name: tstr` gives `name`), or
  `item_<i>` when there is no label, where `i` is the entry's 0-based position in
  the array's flattened group (entries without storage are counted).
- A named group that is spliced in with occurrence 1 becomes one field, named
  after the group rule and typed as the group's struct. An inline parenthesized
  group with occurrence 1 is flattened into the parent. An inline group with any
  other occurrence becomes a field named `group_<i>`.
- Decoding follows the PEG rules. On encode, the generated value is laid out as a
  sequence of items and matched against the same group plan before any output is
  emitted. `[? a: uint, b: uint]` with `a = null` and `b = 5` encodes as `[5]`, and
  the plan would read that `5` as `a`, so `encode` rejects the value with a
  `schema_mismatch` error.

## Maps

| Entry kind | Field name | Storage |
|---|---|---|
| `k: T` | `k` (name transform of the bareword) | Occurrence storage of `T`. |
| `"text": T` or `"text" => T` | Name transform of the text if it is a valid `id`; otherwise `key_<i>` | Occurrence storage of `T`. |
| `n => T` or `n: T` with an integer `n` | `key_<n>`, or `key_neg_<abs(n)>` for a negative `n` | Occurrence storage of `T`. |
| `k => T`, where `k` is a named rule with a single value | Name transform of `k` | Occurrence storage of `T`. |
| Any other literal key (bytes, float, compound) | `key_<i>` | Occurrence storage of `T`. |
| `K => V` with a non-singleton `K` that references a named rule | Name transform of that rule | `[]const struct { key: K', value: V' }` |
| `K => V` with any other non-singleton `K` | `entries`, or `entries_<k>` when there are several | `[]const struct { key: K', value: V' }` |

`<i>` is the entry's 0-based position in the map's flattened group. `<k>` counts
only the unnamed non-singleton-key entries, in order.

- A map whose group is exactly one non-singleton-key entry is stored as the entry
  slice itself: `{ * tstr => uint }` → `[]const struct { key: []const u8, value: u64 }`.
- A literal-key entry occurs at most once (see [standards.md](standards.md#groups-arrays-and-maps)).
  Occurrence `*` or `?` gives `?T`, and `+` gives `T`.
- Non-singleton-key entries are always slices, even with occurrence `?`, and their
  counts are checked. Decoded entries come in ascending order of the keys'
  deterministic encodings.
- Field order follows the source. Wire order is always the deterministic key order,
  whatever the field order is.
- Cuts (`:` and `^ =>`) do not change storage. They change matching only.
- One duplicate-key check runs over every pair the encoder produces. A key in an
  `entries` slice that equals a literal key, or another entry's key, is a
  `schema_mismatch` error.
- An optional group such as `? (lat: float, lon: float)` becomes
  `?struct { lat: f64, lon: f64 }`: both members are present or neither is.

## Choices

A type choice, an augmented socket, or a group enumeration (`&`) is mapped by the
first rule below that applies. The value set is computed after aliases and
references are resolved.

1. The value set is exactly `{false, true}`: `bool`.
2. A `&` enumeration whose members all have singleton values: `enum` named by the
   member labels, with the wire constants generated alongside.
3. Every alternative is integer-valued: an integer, as in [Integers](#integers).
4. Every alternative is float-valued: a float, as in [Floats](#floats).
5. Every alternative is a singleton: `enum`, with a generated table that maps each
   member to its wire constant. The enum's integer tag values are never put on the
   wire.
6. Otherwise: `union(enum)`. Alternatives are not merged, and an alternative that
   references a named choice becomes one arm with that named type.

Arm and enum member names, for the alternative at 0-based position `i`:

1. A reference to a named rule, prelude rules included: the name transform of that
   rule (`uint`, `tstr`, `@"null"`).
2. A text literal that is a valid `id`: the name transform of the text.
3. A group alternative (`//`, or a member of `&`) with exactly one labeled entry:
   the name transform of the label.
4. Otherwise: `alt_<i>`.

If two alternatives end up with the same name, every one of them falls back to
`alt_<i>`.

- Decoding chooses the first alternative that matches. Encoding emits the
  alternative the value holds, then checks that the schema matches the bytes.
  Overlapping alternatives are allowed: with `uint / 1`, the value `.alt_1` encodes
  as `01`, which decodes as `.uint = 1`.
- A group choice (`//`) that makes up a whole array or map body maps that body to a
  `union(enum)` of the alternatives' structs. Inside a group, it becomes a field.
- Absent is not the same as `null`. `? field: uint / null` is stored as
  `field: ?Value = null` with `Value = union(enum) { uint: u64, @"null": void }`.
  The outer `null` means the key is absent, and `.@"null"` means a CBOR `null` was
  sent.

## Tags

| CDDL | Storage |
|---|---|
| `#6.n(T)` | Storage of `T`; the codec owns the tag number. |
| `#6(T)` | `struct { number: u64, content: T' }` |
| `#6.<D>(T)` | `struct { number: N, content: T' }`, where `N` is the integer storage of `D`, checked against `D` |

Nested tags stay nested and are checked from the outside in. A rule whose
definition is another rule wrapped in a tag, or a plain alias, can share its
storage type (`pub const Tagged = Payload;`), but it has its own codec.

## Representation types

| CDDL | Storage | Check |
|---|---|---|
| `#` | `rt.Value` | None. |
| `#0` | `u64` | None. |
| `#0.n`, `n <= 23` | No storage | Equals `n`. |
| `#0.24`, `#0.25`, `#0.26`, `#0.27` | `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64` | None. |
| `#1` | `i65` | `<= -1` |
| `#1.n`, `n <= 23` | No storage | Equals `-1 - n`. |
| `#1.24`, `#1.25`, `#1.26`, `#1.27` | `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i65` | Range `-1 - (2^8 - 1)`, `-1 - (2^16 - 1)`, `-1 - (2^32 - 1)`, or `-2^64` up to `-1`. |
| `#2`, `#2.27`, `#2.31` | `[]const u8` | None. |
| `#2.n`, `n <= 23` | `[n]u8` | None. |
| `#2.24`, `#2.25`, `#2.26` | `[]const u8` | Length at most `2^8 - 1`, `2^16 - 1`, or `2^32 - 1`. |
| `#3`, `#3.n` | `[]const u8` | UTF-8, and the same length rules in bytes. |
| `#4`, `#4.n` | `[]const rt.Value` | Item count, using the same rules. |
| `#5`, `#5.n` | `[]const rt.Value.Entry` | Pair count, using the same rules. |
| `#6` | `struct { number: u64, content: rt.Value }` | None. |
| `#6.n` with no parenthesized content | `rt.Value` | Tag `n`. |
| `#7` | `rt.Value` | Major type 7. |
| `#7.20`, `#7.21`, `#7.22`, `#7.23` | No storage | `false`, `true`, `null`, `undefined`. |
| `#7.n`, `n` in `0..19` or `32..255` | No storage | Simple value `n`. |
| `#7.24` | `u8` | Simple value 32..255. |
| `#7.25`, `#7.26`, `#7.27` | `f16`, `f32`, `f64` | Value exact at that width. |
| `#7.<D>` | `u8` if `D` contains only simple-value numbers, otherwise `rt.Value` | Membership in `D`, read as in RFC 9682 Section 3.2. |

Additional information 28 to 30 on major types 0 through 5, `#0.31`, `#1.31`, and
`#7.28` through `#7.31` denote no data item and are generation errors. For `#6`,
the number is always the tag number (RFC 9682 Section 3.2), never additional
information.

## Controls

| Control | Storage | Codec behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `.size`, `.bits`, `.regexp`, `.lt`, `.le`, `.gt`, `.ge`, `.ne` | Target's storage, narrowed for integers | Checks the predicate. |
| `.eq` with a singleton controller | No storage | Literal. |
| `.and`, `.within` | Target's storage | Checks both operands. When the controller is a container type, the item's encoded bytes are also run through the controller's generated matcher. |
| `.cbor`, `.cborseq` | Target's storage (`[]const u8`) | Bytes are kept unchanged. The embedded item (or sequence) is run through the controller's matcher on both decode and encode. |
| `.default` | Target's storage, inside its optional field | Rejects the default value. See [Defaults](#default). |
| `.plus`, `.cat`, `.det`, `.printf`, `.join` with every element singleton | No storage | Folded literal. |
| `.join` with variable elements | Target's storage | Exact marker-based split; each piece is checked against its element. |
| `.b64u`, `.b64u-sloppy`, `.b64c`, `.b64c-sloppy`, `.b32`, `.h32`, `.hex`, `.hexlc`, `.hexuc`, `.b45`, `.base10`, `.json` | Target's storage (text) | The text stays as it is. Its decoded meaning is checked against the controller's matcher. |
| `.feature` | Target's storage | Matching is unchanged. The use is listed in `features`. |

### Default

```cddl
timer = { time: uint, ? displayed-step: (number .gt 0) .default 1 }
```

```zig
pub const Timer = struct {
    time: u64,
    displayed_step: ?Number = null,
};
// In codecs.Timer:
pub const defaults = struct {
    pub const displayed_step: types.Number = .{ .int = 1 };
};
```

An absent member decodes as `null`; the decoder does not fill in the default. A
present `1` is rejected on decode and on encode, because `.default` implies `.ne`.

### Features

```zig
pub const Feature = struct {
    name: []const u8,
    detail_cbor: ?[]const u8,
    source: []const u8,
    line: u32,
    column: u32,
};
```

There is one entry for each `.feature` occurrence, in source order. `detail_cbor`
holds the deterministic encoding of the `detail` element of a `[name, detail]`
controller, or is `null`. `source` is the input's basename. `line` and `column` are
1-based byte positions.

## Rule kinds, generics, sockets, and recursion

- **Type rule:** one type in `types` and one codec.
- **Group rule:** one struct holding its entries. It is used where the group is
  spliced in. It has no codec of its own, because a group is not a data item.
- **Generic rule:** produces nothing by itself. Each distinct instantiation (the
  generic rule plus its canonical argument values) is emitted once. A rule defined
  as an instantiation (`data = envelope<"data", bstr>`) takes the rule's name. An
  inline instantiation takes `<Generic>_<k>`, where `k` counts that generic's
  inline instantiations in first-encounter order. Rules are visited in source order
  and expressions depth-first, left to right. Instantiations differ whenever their
  arguments differ as schemas: `foo<uint .size 1>` and `foo<uint>` are separate.
- **Sockets:** `$name` maps as the choice of its plugs, in plug order. A socket
  with no plugs is uninhabited (see below).
- **Unwrap:** `~base` inside a container contributes one field named `base`, typed
  as the storage of `Base`, and its entries are spliced on the wire. `~` on a
  tagged type yields the content's storage.
- **Recursion:** inside a strongly connected component of rules, a by-value
  reference (a field, an optional, a union arm, or a fixed array element) to a type
  in the same component becomes `*const T` (or `?*const T`). Slices already provide
  the indirection. `node = { value: int, ? next: node }` becomes
  `struct { value: i65, next: ?*const Node = null }`.
- **Non-productive cycles:** a cycle such as `a = a`, `a = b`, `b = a`, or
  `g = (g)` gets a generation error. A structurally valid type with no finite
  instance, such as `x = [x]`, gets a warning and is still emitted.
- **Uninhabited types:** an empty choice in a position with minimum occurrence 0
  produces no field and matches nothing. In a required position the containing
  type is uninhabited: it is emitted as `enum {}` with a warning, and its codec
  rejects every input.

## Opaque rules

`--opaque <rule>` stores the rule as `rt.Value`. Its codec checks only RFC 8949
well-formedness and validity. Every opaque rule produces a warning on every run,
and no other construct can be made opaque implicitly.

## Round-trip guarantees

- **R1:** If `encode(v)` succeeds, the bytes are in core deterministic encoding,
  the schema matches them, and decoding them and encoding the result gives the same
  bytes.
- **R2:** If no choice in the schema has overlapping alternatives, `decode`
  followed by `encode` returns a value equal to `v`. With overlapping alternatives
  the bytes still round-trip, but the arm may change (see [Choices](#choices)).
- **R3:** If deterministic-input mode accepts input `b`, then `encode(decode(b))`
  returns exactly `b`. In the default mode, a decoded value re-encodes in
  deterministic form: arguments are shortened, indefinite lengths become definite,
  and maps are sorted.

## Worked examples

Map with literal keys:

```cddl
message = { 0: 1, 1: uint, ? 2: tstr, 3: bstr .size 4 }
```

```zig
pub const Message = struct {
    key_1: u64,
    key_2: ?[]const u8 = null,
    key_3: [4]u8,
};
```

`.{ .key_1 = 7, .key_3 = .{ 1, 2, 3, 4 } }` encodes as `a3 00 01 01 07 03 44 01 02 03 04`.
All six orders of the three pairs on the wire decode to the same value. Decoding
rejects a missing key, an unknown key, a duplicate key, the value `2` under key `0`,
and a byte string of 3 or 5 bytes under key `3`.

Record:

```cddl
record = [code: 7, name: tstr, ? enabled: bool, * rest: uint]
```

```zig
pub const Record = struct {
    name: []const u8,
    enabled: ?bool = null,
    rest: []const u64 = &.{},
};
```

`.{ .name = "x", .rest = &.{ 1, 2 } }` encodes as `84 07 61 78 01 02`.

Choice and tag:

```cddl
tagged = #6.42(payload)
payload = "off" / [level: 0..10]
```

```zig
pub const Tagged = Payload;
pub const Payload = union(enum) { off: void, alt_1: u8 };
```

`codecs.Tagged` encodes `.{ .alt_1 = 10 }` as `d8 2a 81 0a`. `codecs.Payload`
encodes `.off` as `63 6f 66 66`. Level 11, a missing tag, a different tag, and
arrays of 0 or 2 items are rejected.

Absent versus null:

```cddl
object = { ? field: value }
value = uint / null
```

```zig
pub const Object = struct { field: ?Value = null };
pub const Value = union(enum) { uint: u64, @"null": void };
```

The three states encode as `a0`, `a1 65 66 69 65 6c 64 f6`, and
`a1 65 66 69 65 6c 64 05` (for `uint = 5`).

Generic instantiation:

```cddl
data = envelope<"data", bstr .size 4>
envelope<kind, body> = [kind, body]
```

```zig
pub const Data = struct { item_1: [4]u8 };
```

`.{ .item_1 = .{ 1, 2, 3, 4 } }` encodes as `82 64 64 61 74 61 44 01 02 03 04`.

Deterministic map order: for keys `100` and `-1`, the encoder emits `18 64` before
`20`, because RFC 8949 Section 4.2.1 orders keys bytewise, not length first.
